What happens when we do not have a plan for misbehavior?
Airplane cartoon

OUTCOMES
Be prepared to categorize misbehaviors as mild/early, moderate, or severe stage 
Begin to analyze if the misbehavior is due to: awareness, ability, attention-seeking, or purposeful/habitual issues
 Be prepared to name a basic correction strategy (approach) for each category.

Severe-Habitual/Long-Standing Problems
When chronic misbehavior does not stem from a student’s lack of awareness or ability, and is not being exhibited because the student wants attention, then  you need to assume that the behavior is now habitual/long standing and is serving some other purpose for the student.
Student loses control/ others may be physically threatened
Teacher doesn’t feel he/she can teach when the student has the problem
Long history of having the problem

Habitual/Long-Standing Problems
Establish a structured system for reinforcing appropriate behavior and providing a consequence for inappropriate behavior
With student create a list of reinforcers
Set up a procedure for monitoring behavior
Create a reinforcement menu
Establish appropriate consequences for misbehavior
Give student increased praise and attention for managing himself/herself well.  
GET ENTHUSISTIC !!!

Moderate Misbehaviors
Gone on for several weeks or for longer intervals of time
Teacher feeling frustrated
Student is always “pushing the boundaries”

Early-Stage Misbehavior
For “Early-Stage” misbehaviors, be prepared to respond with one of a variety of correction strategies that are designed to provide information.
Student is irritating or annoying
Behavior doesn’t interfere with teaching
Student isn’t motivated

Early Stage /Mild Problems
Student should be made aware of the problem 
Set a goal with student to change the behavior 
Respond consistently to the inappropriate behavior
Signals
Verbal Reprimands
Consequence
Use reinforcement to encourage appropriate behavior
Frequent non-contingent attention

Menu of Early-Stage Corrections
Proximity
Gentle verbal reprimand
Discussion
Family Contact
Humor
Praise someone behaving responsibly
Restitution
An emotional reaction
Use planned Ignoring
If behavior is severe and/or affects other students, implement consequences
If other students give the target student attention, gently correct them.
Use reinforcement to encourage appropriate behavior
Use frequent praise and attention
Use intermittent reinforcement
Ensure a 3 to 1 Ratio of positive to negative

Awareness Type Misbehaviors
For ongoing misbehavior that stem from students’ lack of awareness of when/how much they are misbehaving, be prepared to develop and implement an intervention plan that includes increasing their awareness of their behavior.
Awareness Type Misbehaviors

Problems of Ability or Awareness
Conduct Lessons to help the student learn and how to exhibit the appropriate behavior
Make accommodations
Change structure
Develop Goal Contract
Overt Expectations (“No Talking” or “Talking)
Create a limit (tickets, points, etc…)
Teach Self Talk
Create Self Monitoring or Self Evaluation system
Create Prompts
Prompt by using precorrection

Power/Revenge Problems
Respond Consistently 
Clarify difference between positive and negative behavior
Determine a consequence to implement every time the student engages in the negative behavior.
Calmly implement a consequence every time
Don’t show your frustration when the student exhibits the negative behavior – simply invoke the consequence
Identify a positive trait for describing the positive behavior (even the absence of the negative behavior) e.g., “positive leadership”
Praise the student for participating in positive ways
Use the word powerful when describing the plan to the student
Move the student into a position of Positive POWER

Attention –Seeking Problems
Respond Consistently to the inappropriate behavior
Use planned Ignoring
If behavior is severe and/or affects other students, implement consequences
If other students give the target student attention, gently correct them.
Use reinforcement to encourage appropriate behavior
Use frequent praise and attention
Use intermittent reinforcement
Ensure a 3 to 1 Ratio of positive to negative

I’ve Decided To Use Planned Ignoring

What behaviors will I ignore?
What behaviors will I give a corrective consequence?
What behaviors  will I encourage?

  Unfocused with no clear agenda

How do you sell the idea of team planning to frustrated staff members?
TIME

25 Minutes
=
a Plan

Team Members
Leader
Recorder
Time Keeper or Timer
Parent Optional

Background
(Six Minutes)
Describe the problem (when, where, how often, how long, etc… the problem occurs.
Identify student STRENGTHS
Identify strategies already tried
STEP 1:

Problem and Goal
(Two Minutes)
Narrow the scope of the problem and identify a goal.
STEP 2:

Corrective Consequences
(Two Minutes)
Determine whether irresponsible or inappropriate behavior will be corrected, ignored, or whether a consequence will be implemented.
STEP 3:

Responsible and Irresponsible Behavior
(Four Minutes)
Provide examples of responsible and or student strengths to encourage.  Provide examples of irresponsible behavior to discourage.  (T-Chart)
STEP 4:

Proactive Strategies
(Four Minutes)
Brainstorm strategies to encourage responsible behavior (Don’t evaluate).
STEP 5:

Proactive Plan
(Three Minutes)
Select a manageable set of proactive strategies to implement.
STEP 6:

Final Details
(Four Minutes)
Evaluate:  Identify at least two ways to determine if  the plan is working.
Support: Identify things other adults can do to assist the student and teacher.
Plan Summary:  Identify each person’s responsibilities and when actions will be taken.  Identify who will discuss the plan with the student.
STEP 7:

Teamwork = 25 Minutes
Assign roles to members of the group
Leader
Recorder
Time Keeper or Timer
Parent Optional
Read your Background information in your packet (Have one person read orally).  
Complete the 25-minute Intervention Plan for your student
Please put Step 6 & 7 on the Poster-paper under the heading for your student.
